notes.title: Some (good and bad) news - Open letter
notes.content:
Hello merchants!

It's been a while since the game has had an update and information about it. I personally apologize to all those who have had expectations of Merchant Of Phenistoria. To sum up, it's been a difficult year for me, and the game's development has suffered as a result. What's more, since communication isn't my strong point, I wasn't able to express these problems earlier.

Merchant Of Phenistoria is a game close to my heart, a mix of RPG and trading game. The story is part of a much larger lore that I've been working on for years (including a previously published board game). Unfortunately, I didn't have the time, means or energy to continue with this project, resulting in an absence of several months.

My personal situation having improved recently, I'd like to get back to the project a bit more. This doesn't mean, however, that development will resume as before...
On a more technical note, I've started migrating the project from version 3 to 4 of the Godot game engine, offering more resources for 3D (animations, visual effects, performance) and other aspects such as AI pathfinding. Development of the rest of the game will only resume after this migration. I don't want to be too optimistic, so don't expect a new update for a few months yet.

Sincerely,
Aurélien

[i]translation by deepl[/i]

notes.title: Dev diaries 5: The guilds
notes.content:
Hello Merchant!
I'm Proksima and I'm going to tell you about an essential point of the game: the guilds

As explained in the first dev diaries, the heroes are THE main mechanic of the game.
They are the ones who will directly advance the game's story by fighting monsters and completing quests. But since the world is full of danger, the heroes have decided to gather in small communities: the guilds.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39750128/09463d943dc4cd98d5eecd45b8962ced8e4d74fd.png[/img]
[i]Different guilds[/i]


Of course, they will join these guilds according to their affinities: morals, ethics, class, traits....
 The heroes help the development of their guilds by bringing them loot from their quests, money and experience. The guilds will then gain in influence and will become an entity in their own right in the game, so much so that one that is too powerful can become a handicap for you if its intentions are not in line with your ideology.

You will then have to take into account the guilds in your actions and try (or not?) to slow down their progression. For example, a good way is to assassinate one of its members to reduce the stability of the guild, but other more subtle actions can be performed ;)


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39750128/bdb49bd6cf2eea875ace6a00043e38ce8ebcac40.png[/img]
[i]You ask one guild to go and steal from another...[/i]

When a guild has enough experience, it will level up and choose unique skills. Add to this the fact that it will be able to take on more members, if a guild starts buying up the shops and harvesting locations in the city it can become truly unstoppable! But since you are a merchant with a pure heart and a charitable soul, your only wish is to fight monsters and build up the kingdom of Phoenistoria. A guild that is too powerful shouldn't bother you... should it?


As a player, you can also create a mercenary guild by recruiting heroes. You will be able to ask your mercenaries to perform specific actions to help you in your quest.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39750128/b20b29029a5795b61c997392aa828f689dfea5c0.png[/img]
[i]When a guild gains a level, it unlocks a skill according to its alignment[/i]


 If you choose the leadership path, your mercenary guild can even compete with the bigger ones. But you can also skip this step altogether and concentrate on your trade.

It's up to you!

notes.title: Dev Diary 4: Competition and city progress
notes.content:
Hello, merchant!

[h2]Competition[/h2]

You are no longer the only one who can sell equipment to heroes...
Now guilds (especially adventuring guilds) are able to buy stores and supply them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39750128/e81db462d9ca6e01f4cc08b5b7aa06b771bb31bc.png[/img]

Heroes will have to choose a store to buy their favorite equipment. Your reputation (among classes and your alignment) will now have an impact on this decision!

You can now view some sales information in the new city interface

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39750128/cec07b88735be6969ae3d9075badbc4551dfac23.png[/img]


[h2]City Progression[/h2]

The town progression mechanic has been reworked: previously heroes had to complete the first dungeon quest to unlock level 2 of the town. 

We want the player to have more freedom in his evolution (including preventing the success of this quest, which will make sense in a future story update... Thanks for reading this dev diary so far ;-) )

From now on the player will have to accomplish a certain number of objectives to make the city evolve. You can see this information in the new city interface:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39750128/1977d848c983b7e83036b98d83a2f9e545ea2085.png[/img]

notes.title: Devs Diary 03: Factions
notes.content:
Hello, merchant!

We have never been so close to the early access release of the game !
Before the release we would like to introduce you to one of the most important gameplay elements: The Factions

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39750128/7f958336f660a8dd34c536438480a1eda06688d9.png[/img]

There are 4 factions:

- the Church of the Phoenix
- The Cult of Azan
- The Dungeon Master
- The Gnome Tribe

Only one faction controls the city and part of its influence will depend on your actions. Whether it is by interacting directly with her, through the various story quests of the game and through the actions of other heroes and guilds. The faction in power imposes its laws

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39750128/9b453b841f915b4fc7730c3d49d07921a92311fd.png[/img]

In the future, you will be able to directly interact with and influence the game's factions. Also the main story will be directly determined by the factions. We plan to add many quests and dialogues in order to reach the final conclusion: Who will be the owner of the Phoenix egg?

notes.title: Dev Diary 01: Heroes
notes.content:
[h1]Dev Diary 01: Heroes[/h1]

Hello, merchant!

Welcome to our first dev diary !

The town of Phenistoria is inhabited by many heroes who pledge their allegiance to various guilds. Every hero has a unique set of stats and traits that determine their behavior. As a freshly starting merchant, your encounter with heroes will determine your future prosperity. These encounters evolve around one major aspect of the game : reciprocity. The way you choose to play the game will influence the world, and so will affect their behavior. The question is: what kind of merchant do you want to be ?

[h2]Hero traits[/h2]
The new hero traits system will both influence the heroes’ stats and their behaviors.
Each hero will start with some traits (around 3 at the moment) and can lose or gain some during the game.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39750128/5fe4fced1d04f9deb9fe7ad6ef724520d2bbbcc4.png[/img]
[i]Are you sure you want to recruit her?[/i]

We are currently working on a new behavior system. At the moment the system is a binary “if/else” script. We intend to extend it with a “behavior tree” that will provide new interesting combinations.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39750128/540d8873af7badc354a57ff9405fdc2ef0d1b737.png[/img]
[i]Very WIP new behavior tree system and yes, we are using Godot engine[/i]

Soon, heroes will be able to do “actions” (Like “assassination”, “training” or “brawl”...) determined adequately by the new behavior system through the account of the traits and heroes’ alignment (order/neutral/chaos and good/neutral/bad).


Those features are planned to be released in early 2022 (roadmap incoming)


In the next dev diary, we will introduce the guilds.
